Hydroamination of gem-Difluoroallenes
Bao-Xin Liu, Shi-Cun Li, Han-Wen Rao, Qian-Qian Yang,* Wei Du,* and Ying-Chun Chen*

ABSTRACT: We report palladium-catalyzed regiodivergent hydroamination reactions of gem-difluoroallenes. Employing indolines
as the nucleophiles leads to the formation of enantioenriched γ-addition products, while the use of 2-indole-carboxylate-type
substrates switches the selectivity, delivering β-addition E-alkenes exclusively. This protocol provides eficient access to diverse
difluoroalkylated indole derivatives, showing substantial substrate scope and broad functional group compatibility.
gem-Difluoroalkenes and alkanes have gained significant
attention in pharmaceutical chemistry owing to their enhanced
metabolic properties and improved lipophilicity.<sup>1</sup> Among
these, N-difluoropropylindoles and N-difluoroethylindoles
have demonstrated considerable potential for broad bioactiv-
ities, including inhibitors of ASH, MAGL, and PAD, as well as
serving as p53 isosteres (Scheme
1 \mathsf { a } ) . ^ { 2 }
As a result, the
incorporation of difluoroalkyl groups into the indole frame-
works has received growing interest, as it provides valuable
opportunities for the development of novel therapeutic agents.
Traditional methods for the synthesis of gem-difluoroalky-
lated indoles typically employ nucleophilic substitution
reactions between NH-free indoles and halogenated difluor-
oalkenes under basic conditions (Scheme 1b).<sup>3</sup> However, this
approach is not atom-economical, as it results in the loss of a
halogen atom and the use of excess bases. In contrast,
transition metal-catalyzed hydroamination reaction of 1,1-
difluoroallenes ofers an eficient strategy for the introduction
of difluoroallylic groups.<sup>4</sup> Although the reaction is promising,
the asymmetric variants remain limited.<sup>5</sup> Notably, Shi and
Wang developed a rhodium-catalyzed asymmetric hydro-
amination reaction of 1,1-difluoroallenes via exclusive γ-
regioselective addition, whereas only one enantioenriched
difluoroallylated indoline was furnished (Scheme 1c).<sup>6</sup>
With our continuous interest in Pd-catalyzed hydro-
functionalization of unsaturated hydrocarbons,<sup>7</sup> here we
would like to present regiodivergent hydroamination reactions
of 1,1-difluoroallenes by tuning the nucleophiles. This method
enabled the asymmetric synthesis of γ-regioselective adducts
when indolines were used as the nucleophiles, while β-
regioselective products were obtained with the 2-indole-
carboxylate-type substrates. The current strategy ofered a
versatile and eficient approach for constructing diverse
difluoroalkylated indole derivatives, facilitating the rapid
synthesis of structurally varied bioactive analogues.
The initial attempt was conducted by using 1,1-difluor-
oallene 1a and indoline 2a as the model substrates, under the
catalysis of Pd (dba) and L1 [(S)-Segphos)] in toluene at 80
°C (Table 1, entry 1). While product 3a was generated with
exclusive γ-regioselectivity, the reaction sufered from low yield
and enantioselectivity. It was found that product 3a gradually
decomposed during the reaction, giving unidentified side
products. Then a variety of chiral ligands were tested, but
phosphine-based ones generally led to poor yields.<sup>8</sup> In contrast,
using bis(oxazoline) (BOX) ligand L2 provided significantly
improved enantiocontrol (entry 2). Notably, higher reactivity
was observed with indane-derived ligands (L3−5) (entries 3−
5), and a good ee value was obtained with L5 having bulkier
substituents (entry 5). Subsequently, some solvents were
screened (entries 6−9), and DCM turned out to be the
optimal one (entry 6). The reaction still proceeded well at a
lower temperature, and slightly increased enantioselectivity was
gained at
\mathrm { ~ \textit ~ { ~ O ~ } ~ } ^ { \circ } C
(entries 10 and 11). Additionally, a lower
concentration was found to be beneficial for the yield, and the
addition of 4 Å molecular sieves (MS) further improved the
results (entries 12 and 13). Finally, other Pd sources, such as
Pd(PPh ) and Pd(OAc) , proved to be inefective (entries 14
and 15).

To gain more insight into the Pd-catalyzed reactions, some
control experiments were conducted. In the case of γ-
regioselective amination, Pd(II) proved inefective (Table 1,
entry 15), suggesting the reaction is initiated by Pd(0) species.
When deuterium-labeled d-2a was applied to the asymmetric
hydroamination reaction with
\mathrm { P } \hat { \mathrm { d } } _ { 2 } \big ( \mathrm { d } \mathbf { b } \mathbf { a } \big ) _ { 3 } / \mathbf { L } \mathbf { 5 } ,
d-3a was
aforded with 31% D-incorporation, along with recovered
undeuterated 1a (Scheme 5a). Given that indoline 2a is a weak

acid, the related H−Pd species (via oxidative addition) is
unlikely involved in this transformation.<sup>13</sup> As a result, it is
proposed that gem-difluoroallene 1a first coordinates to Pd(0),
followed by protonation<sup>14</sup> with 2a via transition state TS-1 to
generate π-allylpalladium intermediate INT-1, which then is
attacked by indoline anion from the bottom face to aford
product 3a (Scheme 5b).<sup>15</sup> In contrast, the β-regioselective
amination exhibited diferent behavior. When 1a reacted with
d-4a under the catalysis of Pd (dba) /rac-L1, high D-
incorporation at α-site was observed. The results align with a
ligand-to-ligand hydrogen transfer (LLHT) process<sup>16</sup> via TS-2,
forming σ-vinyl-Pd intermediate INT-2, which subsequently
undergoes reductive elimination to yield product 5a.
In conclusion, we have investigated Pd-catalyzed regiodi
vergent hydroamination reactions of gem-difluoroallenes that
demonstrated high nucleophile-dependent regioselectivity,
eficiently constructing two distinct classes of valuable
difluoroalkylated indole derivatives. By employing indolines
as the nucleophiles, enantioenriched γ-addition products were
obtained through a proposed Pd-mediated protonation
pathway followed by asymmetric allylic amination, while 2-
indole-carboxylate-type nucleophiles favored β-addition prod-
ucts likely via a LLHT process. This regiodivergent protocol
provided a versatile synthetic platform for the rapid
construction of structurally diverse difluoroalkylated indole
derivatives, which might be applied as pharmaceutically
relevant scafolds in drug discovery.

regioselective amination, Pd(II) proved inefective (Table 1,
entry 15), suggesting the reaction is initiated by Pd(0) species.
When deuterium-labeled d-2a was applied to the asymmetric
hydroamination reaction with

d-3a was
aforded with 31% D-incorporation, along with recovered
undeuterated 1a (Scheme 5a). Given that indoline 2a is a weak

Mechanism of Hydroamination Reaction
acid, the related H−Pd species (via oxidative addition) is
unlikely involved in this transformation.<sup>13</sup> As a result, it is
proposed that gem-difluoroallene 1a first coordinates to Pd(0),
followed by protonation<sup>14</sup> with 2a via transition state TS-1 to
generate π-allylpalladium intermediate INT-1, which then is
attacked by indoline anion from the bottom face to aford
product 3a (Scheme 5b).<sup>15</sup> In contrast, the β-regioselective
amination exhibited diferent behavior. When 1a reacted with
d-4a under the catalysis of Pd (dba) /rac-L1, high D-
incorporation at α-site was observed. The results align with a
ligand-to-ligand hydrogen transfer (LLHT) process<sup>16</sup> via TS-2,
forming σ-vinyl-Pd intermediate INT-2, which subsequently
undergoes reductive elimination to yield product 5a.
In conclusion, we have investigated Pd-catalyzed regiodi
vergent hydroamination reactions of gem-difluoroallenes that
demonstrated high nucleophile-dependent regioselectivity,
eficiently constructing two distinct classes of valuable
difluoroalkylated indole derivatives. By employing indolines
as the nucleophiles, enantioenriched γ-addition products were
obtained through a proposed Pd-mediated protonation
pathway followed by asymmetric allylic amination, while 2-
indole-carboxylate-type nucleophiles favored β-addition prod-
ucts likely via a LLHT process. This regiodivergent protocol
provided a versatile synthetic platform for the rapid
construction of structurally diverse difluoroalkylated indole
derivatives, which might be applied as pharmaceutically
relevant scafolds in drug discovery.
